newsitem.title: CONGO: Shooting after dark in Brazzaville after calm day.
newsitem.headline: Shooting after dark in Brazzaville after calm day.

text.p: A sustained outbreak of firing shattered the evening calm around the international airport in the capital of the former French colony of Congo on Friday after a day of relative calm, witnesses said.
But the barrage, sustained small arms fire as well as mortars and rocket propelled grenades, was not as heavy as during earlier evenings in the standoff, the witnesses added.

The bloody standoff, which pits supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and against those of his predecessor, former Marxist military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso, began on June 5 after the army surrounded Sassou Nguesso's Brazzaville home.
Lissouba and his government ordered the move as part of efforts to crack down on private militias ahead of a planned July 27 presidential election.
Friday was comparatively quiet despite sporadic shooting and explosions in the city. Mediators raised the prospect of peace talks in Gabon hosted by its president, Omar Bongo.
